home.hook: Made with AI. Lost in the chat.
home.subhead: One workspace for you, your people, and the AI you already use. Nothing to set up — and every change signed by whoever made it, human or not.
home.problemTitle: The real work happens with AI now — in a window only you can see.
home.problemA: Drafts, decisions, analysis — the actual thinking happens in an AI chat. And then it's gone: scrolled past, unfindable next week, invisible to the people it was made for.
home.problemB: Getting it in front of anyone else is still copy-paste. You do the work with AI, then you ferry it — into a doc, into a thread, into an email — by hand, every time.
home.recognitionQuote: I'm the human clipboard between my AI and my team.
home.recognitionAnswer: If that's you, this is the fix.
home.productTitleA: Dedicated apps, a shared file system,
home.productBody: Everything below ships with the workspace. Connect your AI and it works in the same apps, on the same files, under its own name.
home.proofEyebrow: The part no one else can show you
home.proofTitle: Every change, signed by whoever made it.
home.proofA: You on Tuesday. Your agent on Thursday. Claude on Friday. One file, three authors — and you can walk every line back to who wrote it, when, and why.
home.proofB: A single-vendor tool structurally can't draw this picture: it only ever sees itself. A shared workspace where everyone — you, your people, your AI — signs their own work is the one place the whole story exists.
home.insightTitle: The AI will change. Your record shouldn't.
home.insightBody: New models show up every few months, and each one is better than the last. What lasts isn't any one of them — it's the signed record of the work: what was decided, what was corrected, who did what. Keep that in one place you own, and every new model makes your workspace more valuable, not less. Ninety days in, starting over anywhere else means starting from zero.
home.whereTitle: A shared workspace, not a black box.
home.whereA: Your files are never training data — not for us, not by default for the models we call. When you ask an AI to work, the relevant files go to that provider to do the job, and we name every provider we can send them to.
home.whereB: Nothing here deletes itself on a timer. Every change is signed by whoever made it, every version is kept, and the whole workspace exports as a plain git repo you can walk offline.
home.whereLink: Read the details — including what we don't have
home.pricingTitle: Free for two. A seat for the rest.
home.pricingBody: The workspace is free for you and a teammate — your files, your record, reachable from any AI you use. From the 3rd person, each extra seat is paid; usage is pay-as-you-go from one shared balance. AI connections are always free — never a seat.

files.title: One shared file system — every change signed.
files.body: You, your people, and every AI you connect write into the same place. Every write carries a name — You, a teammate, ChatGPT — every version is kept, and any file can be walked back revision by revision.

agents.title: Agents ready out of the box.
agents.body: Every app comes with its own colleague — an editor for your decks and documents, a designer for your images, a blogger for what you publish. Ask any of them to keep a file current and it runs on the contract you set. They work on your files as you, with every edit under your name and kept in the file's history. You meet them where the work is, from the first minute.

meta.description: How yarnnn differs from ChatGPT and Claude's built-in memory, what 'trace' is, how co-work with your AIs and your team actually lands, pricing, and how to get started.

memory.q: How is this different from ChatGPT or Claude's memory?
memory.a: Their memory is walled to their own app — you can't read inside it, version it, or take it with you. yarnnn is a shared workspace that lives outside any single AI: every model you connect works in the same files you do, every change is signed and dated — human or not — and it's all yours to export. Write it with Claude, and it's there when you open ChatGPT.

mine.a: Yes. Every file carries its author's name, every version is kept, and the whole thing exports as a plain git repo with its history intact. We never train on it — and nothing here deletes itself on a timer.

trace.a: Trace shows how any fact changed over time — who changed it, when, and what it was before. It's the thing a plain storage connector or an app's built-in memory can't show you: the full history behind what your AI knows.

team.q: Does it work across my team, not just me?
team.a: Yes — share a link or invite by email and a teammate lands in the same shared workspace. You, your people, and your AIs all work in the same files, every change signed with its author's name, and you can narrow or revoke anyone's access at any time. Two people work free.

inout.q: How do I put things in, and get them out?
inout.a: Tell any connected AI to remember something, upload your files and notes, or connect the tools you already use (Slack, Notion). Any other AI — or teammate — can then recall it on the next session — no copy-paste, no re-explaining who you are.

models.q: Which AI models does it work with?
models.a: Any that speak MCP — ChatGPT, Claude, and others. It's neutral on purpose: it isn't tied to any one model, which is exactly why it can sit across all of them.

where.q: Where does my work go when I ask an AI to do something?
where.a: To the model provider running that task — Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, or DeepSeek, depending on which model is picked. They process it to answer, and under their API terms none of them train on it by default. File text also goes to OpenAI to build the search index that makes your workspace findable. The full list of everyone who can receive your data is on the data page.

cando.q: What can a connected AI actually do in my workspace?
cando.a: The same things you can: read, write, move, delete, and share files. It connects through OAuth you approve and can revoke, and every change it makes is signed with its name — so you can always see what it did and walk it back. Connect assistants you trust.

cost.a: Your memory is free for two people — your files, your context, reachable from any AI. Pricing has two axes: seats and usage. The first two seats (you and a teammate) are free; each person from the 3rd onward is a paid seat ({seat}/mo), and AI connections are always free — never a seat. Usage is pay-as-you-go from one shared balance the owner funds; top up any amount from {topUpMin} (top-ups never expire). Every workspace starts with a {signupGrant} balance to feel the loop before you spend a cent.

cap.q: Can I cap what it spends?
cap.a: Yes. Spend is bounded by the balance itself — usage is pay-as-you-go, so nothing can draw more than you've put in, and the hard stop at zero pauses the work without losing anything. On a team, the owner can additionally set a per-member spend cap on the shared balance.

runout.q: What if my balance runs out, or I turn the assistant off?
runout.a: Nothing is deleted. When the balance is spent, the assistant pauses — top up to resume. Turn it off and it simply stops drawing usage. Either way, your memory and every file stay yours, free.

howstart.a: Start free. Connect an AI tool over MCP (or upload files, or just start typing), tell it something worth keeping, and watch it show up in the next AI you open — with the full history intact.

desktop.a: Yes, for Mac and Windows, free on every plan. It's the same workspace in its own window. It's in beta, so the first time you open it your computer asks you to confirm; the download page shows how. Everything also works in any browser.

firstmove.a: Connect the two AIs you use most, and save one thing in one of them. Open the other and recall it. That round-trip — write once, there everywhere, fully traceable — is the whole idea in about thirty seconds.

stage.a: Yes. It works and we run our own work on it every day, but it will keep changing, and some things will break along the way. None of that touches your files: every version is kept, every change is signed, and the whole workspace exports as a plain git repo whenever you like. If something breaks or confuses you, use Send feedback in your account menu.

browser.q: Can my agent act on websites for me?
browser.a: Yes — in your own Chrome, through the yarnnn extension, from yarnnn on the web or the desktop app. Your agent works in tabs of its own with the sign-ins you already have, and asks before it uses a site for the first time. It acts while you're there to watch: work you want repeated waits for you to start it. Banking, payments, trading and password managers are never allowed.

developers.verbsIntroA: File-native: they read and write the same files a person sees, and every write lands under its author's name. Documented in full in the

verb.whoami: Name where you are standing — which workspace this connection is bound to, who your writes will be signed as, and which verbs your token authorizes. Call it before writing somewhere the user assumed.
verb.open: Read one exact file: its current content, who last changed it, when, and its recent signed revisions. An unknown path says so — open never guesses.
verb.list: Enumerate the files under a folder. Takes a timestamp for the change feed — what moved since you were last here — and pages through large subtrees.
verb.search: Find files by meaning. Returns ranked matches with excerpts and a confidence signal, so an ambiguous result can be asked about rather than guessed at.
verb.history: Show how one exact file changed over time — who authored each revision, when, what changed, and a diff against its predecessor. The capability a plain storage connector cannot show.
verb.runs: Read what the workspace's agents did — the run ledger, newest first: a standing run, or the acts an agent performed in a member's own browser, each step with where the tab was when it ended, what it acted on, and whether anything changed. The executor's receipts, never the model's account. Read-only and idempotent.
verb.save: Write a file back as a signed revision. Pass the revision you opened and a concurrent change is refused rather than clobbered; every prior version stays on the chain.
verb.edit: Change part of a file by anchoring on its exact current text. Only the change travels, so content you never read is never at risk — the right verb for large files.
verb.delete: Remove a file from the live workspace. Nothing is lost: the chain keeps the content and the file can be restored.
verb.move: Move or rename a file. Refuses to overwrite an existing destination — that has to be deleted by intent first.
verb.request_upload: Get a short-lived URL for content that arrives as bytes rather than text — an image, a PDF, an export. It lands as a signed file like any other.
verb.share: Mint a link to one file or the whole workspace, as full access or read-only. Whoever opens it sees the work and who made it.

developers.scopesIntroA: Access is scoped per verb and enforced on every call — a token holding
developers.scopesIntroB: is refused when it tries to save. The tiers are additive, and a registration that names none gets read-only.

scope.read: Read your files — open, list, search, view their history — and what your agents did (runs).
scope.write: Create, edit, move, and delete files. Every change is signed and revertible.
scope.share: Create share links, which can give whoever opens them full member access.
